key_insight: Multi-material topology optimization designs phononic crystals with widened elastic-wave bandgaps or bandgaps aligned to a user-defined frequency range.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports frequency-selective vibration isolation and elastic-wave filtering through engineered periodic material layouts.
method: Compute dispersion bands using Floquet–Bloch theory and finite-element eigenvalue analysis along the irreducible Brillouin-zone boundary.
Interpolate effective density and stiffness from design weights for multiple candidate materials.
Optimize adjacent-band separation with auxiliary bounds, or target a frequency range using adaptive band pairing.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation of optimized bandgap performance against transmission-loss spectra computed in COMSOL Multiphysics, but provides no quantitative results.
watch_item: Repeated finite-element eigenvalue solves may be computationally costly; no learned surrogate or experimental validation is described in the abstract.
paper_title: Multi-Material Topology Optimization of Phononic Crystals for Targeted Elastic Wave Bandgap
